name: v0.3.6
body:
Hotfix for 0.3.5: the viewer did not load. If you installed 0.3.5, run the install line again to update.

### Fixed
- **The viewer loads again.** 0.3.5 shipped with a typo in one script that stopped the whole app starting: no tabs, Browse did nothing and dropped models downloaded instead of opening. A test now parses every viewer script, so this cannot ship again.
- **A `.provenance.json` beside the GLB is kept.** With Debug off, the viewer deleted everything but the GLB, licence record included; the record now stays with the file.

Pixel Match and everything else from 0.3.5 is unchanged: https://github.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/releases/tag/v0.3.5

name: v0.3.5
body:
**Pixel Match.** Normally, Image-to-3D models redraw your picture, and the fine stuff (text, logos, numbers, faces) can come back as garbled or scuffed on your model. Pixel Match fixes that, making the output look near pixel-identical. Eg: Text like "VANGUARD 07" stays "VANGUARD 07" as in the demo video.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b0189b1-5f7d-48ae-a960-77fe754d4ec3


Pair it with a low-poly finish: ~900k faces down to ~5k, and the front still matches your picture. On by default in **Finish** for Pixal3D models made in the lab. More backends and more angles are coming next.

## Also new

- **Finish works on NVIDIA.** Linux tested end to end on an RTX 3090; Windows should work the same way. Finish needs **Blender 4.2+**, which you install yourself ([blender.org](https://www.blender.org/download/)). Setup & Status now shows whether it's found.
- **Finish no longer repaints by default.** Pixal3D models arrive painted and Pixel Match keeps the front exact, so a finish takes seconds, not minutes, and needs no extra download. Want the sides and back redrawn too? Tick **Also repaint the sides and back** (Apple Silicon for now, needs the 8.7 GB Hunyuan paint weights).
- **Before and after in Finish**, cameras locked together. Plus a 5k-triangle preset and tidier run folders: the finished model sits on its own at the top, named after your model and its size, and the in-between steps are tucked into a `steps` folder.
- **Compare shows up to four models** in a grid.
- **Pixal3D setup brings the BiRefNet-lite background remover** along, so thin and light-coloured parts survive the cut-out.
- **Rebuild button** in Setup & Status for Pixal3D installs that predate our latest fixes. No Terminal needed.

## Fixes

- **Hunyuan3D-MLX paint works on a fresh install.** Thanks @gabelul for the report (#65).
- **Mac-only backends point NVIDIA users somewhere.** TRELLIS.2 and Hunyuan3D now link their official NVIDIA versions instead of a bare "needs Apple Silicon".
- **TRELLIS.2 warns about its gated DINOv3 encoder up front**, so nobody waits out a 14 GB download to hit a login error.
- Restarting the viewer no longer kills a Finish run another process is running.
- The viewer no longer quotes run times measured on our machines. Yours will differ.

## Update

Run the same install line again:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.sh | bash
```

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then open **Setup & Status**:

- **Already have Pixal3D but not the background remover?** Pixal3D shows **Resume download**. It fetches just the 224 MB remover.
- **Want Finish?** Install Blender 4.2+ if the Blender card says it's missing, then restart the viewer.

name: v0.3.4
body:
**Standardised background removal.** u2net wasn't cutting it. Literally. So we've upgraded to BiRefNet-lite, which is blazing fast. Took a sec to load on my mac and ~4 secs for clean-up. It's an extra download (224 MB), but it gives the models much cleaner input images, and it now runs for every backend.

Get it from **Setup & Status → Background remover**. Until you do, runs use u2net as before.

## Optimisations

- **Pixal3D runs 8 sampling steps instead of 12.** 15–30% faster in our tests, same shape. Pick **12 (full)** under Steps for hero assets.

## Fixes

- **Pixal3D only offers 1024.** Its single-image mode doesn't support 1536, so picking it failed straight away.
- **The Generate 3D preview shows just your model**, not the whole viewer squeezed into the panel.

## Changes

- Generated images now save to `output/images/`.

## Update

Run the same install line again:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.sh | bash
```

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then, optionally:

- **New background remover:** Setup & Status → Background remover → Set up. (From a terminal: `cd ~/image-to-3dlab && .venv/bin/python scripts/bootstrap_matte.py`.)
- **Faster Pixal3D (Mac):** open **Terminal** (⌘+Space, type "Terminal"), paste this and press Enter:

  ```bash
  cd ~/image-to-3dlab && .venv/bin/python scripts/bootstrap_pixal3d.py --build-only --rebuild
  ```

  It takes a couple of minutes and downloads no models. Restart the viewer afterwards. Same command on Linux with the CUDA toolkit. Windows stays at 12 steps for now. (Installed somewhere other than `~/image-to-3dlab`? Use that folder instead.)

name: v0.3.3
body:
**Windows + NVIDIA: your GPU gets used now.** The installer was pulling the CPU-only PyTorch (the only one PyPI has for Windows), so everything ran on the processor. It now installs PyTorch with CUDA, and re-running the installer replaces a CPU-only build. Reported by @paisanllc in #50. This one is pending verification on real Windows machines, so if you try it, please tell us how it went.

Also in this release:

- **Finish bakes the original's detail** onto the finished model: a normal map (the fine relief a retopology throws away) and the source's metallic-roughness map, so metal stays shiny and skin stays matte. New "Bake detail" stage, a few seconds long; `--skip-bake` turns it off. Flagged by @AdrielSantana in #49.
- **Pixal3D writes a run record** (`<model>.json` beside the GLB) with the input image, settings, licence and file hashes, like the other routes. Reported by @paisanllc in #50.

## Update

Run the same install line again:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.sh | bash
```

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

name: v0.3.2
body:
**NVIDIA driver 610+ works again.** Newer drivers renamed the CUDA field that `nvidia-smi` prints, so Setup couldn't read your CUDA version and refused every model. Found and diagnosed by @paisanllc in #50. Thank you!

Also in this release:

- **Apache-2.0 licence**, with a `NOTICE` file. Model weights keep their own licences.
- **Qwen-Image wording:** the pictures you generate are yours, per Qwen's statement. The licence text itself is ambiguous, so commercial users should check it themselves.
- **Fresh installs** now include the mesh libraries (`trimesh`, `fast_simplification`, `rtree`).

## Update

name: v0.3.0 — now runs on NVIDIA Linux
body:
Text > image > 3D, now on a Linux machine with an NVIDIA card as well as on Apple Silicon.

- **Images** (Qwen-Image) via stable-diffusion.cpp's Vulkan build.
- **3D** via Pixal3D and Stable Fast 3D on CUDA.
- Tested on an **RTX 4090**, **RTX 3090 Ti** and **RTX 3090** (Ubuntu 24.04, cloud GPUs). Linux desktop and Windows testers welcome in Discussions.

## Install (or update) in one line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/main/install.sh | bash
```

Run the same line again later to update. It installs the code and Python, then tells you how to start the lab. **It downloads no model weights.** You pick what to install in the viewer's Setup & Status page, which shows the size and licence first and asks before fetching anything.

## What's new

- **NVIDIA Linux support** for Generate Image, Pixal3D and Stable Fast 3D.
- **Pixal3D picks its build for your machine.** With the CUDA toolkit it compiles for your card (a few minutes, once). Without it, it uses the prebuilt CUDA build (driver 575+).
- **One-line installer and updater** (`install.sh`; `install.ps1` for Windows, untested).
- **Update banner:** the viewer tells you when a new release is out (once a day at most; turn it off on the About page or with `I3D_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`).
- **About page** with your machine, the routes it can run, and what's new.
- **No silent CPU runs:** if image generation can't reach the GPU, it stops and tells you the fix instead of taking many minutes per picture.

## Things we hit on real NVIDIA machines (all fixed or handled)

- **Stable Fast 3D could turn the background into geometry.** SF3D skips background removal whenever an image has a transparency channel, assuming it's already cut out. But an image can carry that channel with nothing in it actually transparent, and then the backdrop gets built into the model along with the subject. SF3D's default doesn't cover that edge case; we now check whether anything is really transparent, and remove the background ourselves if not.
- **Headless Linux boxes** lack the graphics libraries Vulkan needs. Setup catches this before downloading anything and prints the fix: `apt install libegl1 libgl1`. Hopefully your daily driver won't need it. BUT this also means you can run this headlessly on the cloud.
- **Older drivers** (below 575) can't run the prebuilt Pixal3D; it compiles instead, or says which driver to install.
- **CUDA toolkit older than PyTorch's CUDA:** SF3D now falls back to a CPU texture baker (about 15 s a model on a 3090 Ti, so you won't notice).
- **Many-core, low-memory containers:** Pixal3D's compile ran out of memory; it now sizes its job count to the memory really available. Again, this shouldn't matter to you if this is your daily driver, but in case you run it in the cloud, it's taken care of.

## Known issues

- Windows is wired up but not yet tested. Reports welcome in Discussions.
- The background-removal step prints TensorRT/CUDA warnings on Linux, then runs on the CPU. They look alarming; they are harmless.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#030---2026-09-24).

name: v0.2.0 — you no longer need a picture to start
body:
Two months of work. The headline is that the pipeline grew a step at the front: it used to
assume you already had a source image, and now it can make one.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b15f7d9-1675-4966-a28b-28164010be69


### Type a prompt, get a 3D model

A **Generate Image** tab now sits before Generate 3D. It runs Qwen-Image 2.1 locally
through `stable-diffusion.cpp` on Metal — no account, no API key, nothing leaves your
machine. Hand the result straight to Generate 3D. 

Its weights are **non-commercial** (Qwen Research License), and that restriction carries
into anything you build from the picture, including the mesh. The viewer says so before it
downloads anything, and the outputs are sorted into a `research_only/` folder so you never
have to open a file to find out which ones are restricted.

### A new best backend

**Pixal3D** (C++/GGML, Metal) is now the recommended route: one pass, no separate repaint
stage, about six minutes on the test asset. It joins TRELLIS.2, Stable Fast 3D and two
Hunyuan3D-MLX routes — five backends behind one interface.

### TRELLIS.2 got 2.4x faster

An MLX attention backend takes a 1024-resolution run from **34.3 minutes to 14.3** on my m5 macbook. 
It is optional and off by default; the viewer checks whether it can be enabled and says so
rather than failing partway through a run.

### The viewer installs things for you

A **Setup & Status** page shows every backend, what it needs, how many gigabytes that is
and under what licence — and waits for an answer. Nothing is ever downloaded because you
clicked something that sounded generic. It is now the only place a download can start.

### Finishing, in the browser

Retopology and repaint run as a job you can watch, cancel and resume. 

### Also - some QoL

- Normal-map baking works 
- A visual README that opens on real source images and the models made from them
- Windows and non-Apple machines are told a backend cannot run there, instead of failing
  with a raw `[WinError 2]`

---

## About the timings

**Every number above is on Apple Silicon Mac.** A faster chip does better and an NVIDIA
card is in a different league — a ten-minute generation here is under a minute there. If
you run this, please post your times in Discussions; the project currently has exactly one
machine's picture of itself.

---

## Watch this repo & Follow me

Follow me on x.com/bingeljell for more real time updates.

If you like the repo, please star it. If you want to hear about releases:
**Watch → Custom → Releases**. That is the only way GitHub will tell you. 

**Full changelog:** CHANGELOG.md

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
